_authority: The ordered pipeline and who owns each step. SKILL.md points here and must not restate the order in prose.
_revised: 2026-09-10 - the visual layer became an explicit required step (8) owned by course-module-ui, and its audit joined verify. Before this the pipeline named no owner for how a module LOOKS, so a module could pass every UX check and still ship as default white HTML. Steps renumbered from 8 onwards. | 2026-09-10 (Phase 3) - a VISUAL PLAN step (9) owned by course-visuals was inserted after the visual system and before task pages, and course-visuals joined verify. Before this the pipeline named an owner for how a module LOOKS but none for WHAT THE PICTURE SHOULD BE, so a module could pass every check and still ship card grids and boxes joined by arrows. Steps renumbered from 9 on. | 2026-09-11 - a RETROFIT pipeline was added beside the build pipeline. The steps are not the same: a retrofit starts from existing material, so it classifies the delivery first and its content steps are reads rather than writes.

steps.does: Stage 1. Look in the folder first; sort the knowledge base's sources (kb_tool.py sources - exact copies, format copies, editions); ask what is still missing in one batch of pop-up questions - programme, knowledge base, old course, course type, model course and language only if not found, which edition is current; record everything in _factory/intake.json
steps.blocked_without: nothing - the programme is the one blocking ANSWER, and it is asked here
steps.output: _factory/intake.json, _factory/kb_sources.json, and COURSE_STATE.md + FEEDBACK_LOG.md started (scripts/course_memory.py start) with the course table and every intake decision filled in
steps.added: 2.13.0 (Phase 5 step 2). Numbered 0 so no later step moves.

steps.does: transcribe the approved topic/hours table; read the academic-hour length off the programme
steps.output: programme.json, reconciled against the table's own total row

steps.does: transcribe the IMO model course's detailed syllabus - its Knowledge, Understanding and Proficiency column - one row per item, its own numbering as the id. These are the itemised outcomes the programme's topics only summarise.
steps.blocked_without: the model course document behind the programme
steps.why: the programme gives topics; the model course gives the outcomes INSIDE each topic. A course can cover every topic and still miss outcomes, and only this transcription lets that be checked. Transcribe, never summarise: the value is that the wording is the model course's own.

steps.does: sources for the subject, extracted and searchable - a Course Source Processor knowledge base or an older docling one, told apart by their files. Searched with kb_tool.py search; retrieval packs are written into the course folder's _factory/retrieval/, never into the knowledge base. Only the current edition of a publication is cited (intake).
steps.note: search the extracted text before declaring a source unreadable; never read a document.md or content.md whole

steps.does: Main ILOs verbatim; Sub-ILOs re-expressed for digital/practical delivery, each marked PROVISIONAL
steps.rule: never renumber a Sub-ILO anywhere a trainee can see

steps.does: L41 (owner, 2026-10-01): every file of the old course read - slides, exercises, handouts, tests, films - and every picture copied out; then, per module, what is kept, modernised and made digital, and added. It is the foundation the architecture is planned from.

one module per programme topic, in the programme's order (L34, 2.17.0) - the final-assessment topic is the last module, assessment only; sum each module's allocated minutes. (Before 2.17.0: assign topics to modules and declare the topics outside them.)

Stage 2 STOP: write architecture.json beside programme.json and plan.json, run scripts/make_architecture_page.py --check, then write ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.html and STOP. The page shows every module - one per programme topic (L34), the final assessment last - with its hours and where its minutes go, how the course runs on the two tablets (L35), the Main ILOs verbatim, every Sub-ILO beside the programme wording (kept / re-expressed / added), active learning, practical tasks with equipment and the test plan. The operator's 'next' approves it and ratifies the Sub-ILO changes.
steps.why: changing a table row is free; changing eight built modules is not

steps.does: Stage 3 STOP, per module: the exact words of every screen in trainee order - one task per screen - with the planned picture, instructor notes, every question with answers, correct answer and feedback, and the operator-stated facts listed once. A review page and a Word file for the operator. Every correction is shown as an understood list before it is applied (apply --confirmed only after the operator says yes). The final-assessment bank the same way (--module final).
steps.added: 2.16.0 (Phase 5 step 5). Numbered 6b so no later step moves.

steps.does: per module, the ordered list of screens with kind and purpose - DERIVED from the approved content script (6b), not approved separately. Every screen built from it carries data-script=<id>.

establish the module's visual layer BEFORE any HTML: run course-module-ui/scripts/design_system.py install <module> --start-deck, which copies every canonical style file and engine into the module's assets/ byte for byte - the files are copied, never read - then read course-module-ui/references/vocabulary.md, the full list of compositions, components and tokens by name and when to use each. Every colour, radius, shadow and font in new work comes from a token.
steps.blocked_without: the screen inventory approved at step 7
steps.rule: REQUIRED for every new module - the visual layer is not optional and is not course-module-ux's to invent. A new deck that hardcodes its own colours has started a second visual dialect.
steps.why: course-module-ux is a floor (contrast, tap size, fill, overflow), not an identity. Two modules can pass every check in floor.json and look nothing alike - that already happened across the eight GAS BASIC modules. Routing the look to its owner is what stops it happening again.
steps.reference: GAS BASIC Module_01 is the canonical visual reference. Canonical means the LOOK - palette, typography, light/dark-photo modes, header band, card geometry, pills, spacing, radius, shadow, takeaway treatment, semantic status colour. It is NOT a template: see no_fixed_slide_count.
steps.applies_to: the deck screens, and the shared token layer the task pages and handout draw from

steps.does: per important concept: name the LEARNING NEED, choose the representation, decide the source strategy, and answer the four animation questions where anything moves. Output is an approved visual storyboard (templates/VISUAL_STORYBOARD.md). Deciding NO visual is a recorded outcome.
steps.blocked_without: the screen inventory (7) and the visual system (8)
steps.rule: REQUIRED for a substantial module, any complex concept, anything animated and anything needing a new asset. NOT required for a single labelled photograph or a plain-text screen.
steps.why: course-module-ui fixes the palette and course-module-ux fixes the geometry; neither decides whether a concept should be a photograph, a schematic, an animation or a sentence. That decision is where generic AI course graphics come from.
steps.also: runs the asset pipeline levels 1-2 (scripts/resolve_asset.py) so a screen is never designed around a photograph that does not exist; emits RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED and GENERATED_ASSET_REQUIRED rather than shipping quietly.

steps.does: the trainee task pages the screens will announce
steps.rule: BEFORE the deck announces them - a screen announcing a task the tablet lacks is the worst failure in the room

steps.does: the one-page module: open, Start, Next to the end
steps.rule: the deck announces a task and never launches it

steps.does: the trainee's take-home, AND the overflow valve for anything that will not fit the accredited minutes
steps.rule: every moved item recorded in the companion file with its source topic

steps.does: the final assessment, separate from every module check; the programme's own question count and pass mark
steps.rule: no answer key on a trainee page; a re-sit needs a different paper

steps.does: one plan per module, stating its allocated and built minutes on its own face
course pack into the trainee terminal; plans, prepare and record into the instructor terminal; regenerate the run script
steps.rule: no app code, no forked terminal, no copied shared engine

steps.does: run every check and READ the output: hours, model-course outcome coverage, structure, links, navigation reachability, task crosscheck, and the visual audit of the module's own stylesheets. A green exit is not proof the work happened - inspect the line for the thing you changed.
steps.rule: a green exit is not proof; read the line for the thing you changed
scripts: course-module-ui/scripts/design_system.py check <module>   (NEW modules only - the copied style files are identical)
steps.why_two_were_added: check_syllabus_coverage.py and audit_navigation.py were added 2026-09-07 because every other check passed on a course that was missing an accredited outcome (IMO 1.04 item 9.2.7) and shipping a 28-page section nothing linked to.
steps.visual_signoff: A new module is not signed off until course-module-ui/scripts/audit_ui.py has been run over its stylesheets with --strict and read. --strict is correct for new work and WRONG for shipped material: never point it at an already-delivered GAS BASIC or Electrical Technician module. Existing modules carry known drift (course-module-ui/SKILL.md records it) - report it, name the files, and leave the repaint to the owner. The purpose is that new work does not start a new visual dialect, not that history gets repainted.
steps.visual_teaching_signoff: course-visuals/review/GUIDE.md - the half no script can do. A visual does not pass because the HTML validates, the links work and the CSS fits. Fourteen named failure modes and one question: does this actually teach? Nothing at RIGHTS_REVIEW_REQUIRED may ship.

steps.does: write factory-notes.md into the course folder - what was produced, every marker, the achieved ratio, what moved to the handout, and feedback on this skill

memory._law: L32 (2.14.0). Every stage ends by updating COURSE_STATE.md - the stage, what was approved, open questions, the next step, the file map - and running scripts/course_memory.py check. Every operator correction is written into FEEDBACK_LOG.md when it is made. A session that opens a course folder with a COURSE_STATE.md reads it first and does not re-ask or re-decide anything under 'Decided'.
memory.at_the_end: When the operator says they are happy with the finished course: course_memory.py draft-pattern, show the draft to the operator in plain language, let them change or remove any point, and only on their approval course_memory.py approve-pattern --by <name>.

non_negotiable_orderings: the GATE (6) before anything is built (7+)
hours (1) and the ILO map (4) before the module split (5) is believed
the model-course syllabus (2) is transcribed before the GATE, because the module split has to be able to say which module carries which outcome - not only which topic
screen inventory (7) before any screen exists (11)
the visual system (8) before any screen exists (11), so the first screen is already tokenised - retro-fitting tokens onto a finished deck is how drift gets signed off
task pages (10) before the deck announces them (11) - a screen announcing a task the tablet lacks is the worst failure in the room
the visual audit runs at verify (16), never against a shipped module
the visual plan (9) before any figure is implemented - jumping from text straight into HTML is where card grids and box-and-arrow chains come from
the asset pipeline is searched before a screen is designed around an asset (9), so a layout is never built around a photograph that does not exist

roles.course-factory: programme, hours law, build order, ILO immutability, ratio rule, traceability, terminal contract
roles.course-module-ux: one-page module behaviour, screen architecture, fill, overflow, instructor delivery UX, deck measurement, run-script generation
roles.course-module-ui: the visual identity derived from GAS BASIC Module_01 - tokens, the two slide modes, header band, cards, pills, photo, takeaway, semantic status colour. The LOOK only
roles.course-task-ux: trainee task behaviour and usability - answering, navigation, typed input, completion
roles.course-tablet-publisher: publication to the trainee and instructor terminals and the shared repository
roles.novikontas-*: intake, course plan document, COURSE_START contract, pedagogy, exercise forms, handouts, written tests, corporate brand
roles.course-visuals: what representation teaches a concept; the instructional-animation law (L13); the four-level asset pipeline, provenance, licences and rights (L12); the visual quality gate

no_fixed_slide_count: There is NO canonical screen count. A module's screen count is derived from the learning need, the delivery method, the content depth, the practical work, the activities and what actually has to be explained - a legitimate module may be 10 screens, 25, 50, almost no presentation, or practical-only. Module_01 is a quality and UX/UI reference, not a numeric template. Never add filler screens to resemble it numerically, and never cut real teaching to resemble it either. What must match across modules is the SYSTEM: visual language, UI quality, UX behaviour, tablet-first delivery, the Start -> Next -> Next one-page delivery model where it applies, component styling, responsive behaviour, visual hierarchy, task usability and functional quality.
density_is_not_depth: Low visible density does not mean low learning depth, and not every screen has to be interactive. Progressive disclosure, layered cards, diagrams, animation and interactive figures can carry serious teaching depth without a wall of text - 'compact' (course-module-ux law 3) must never be read as 'almost no teaching content'. course-module-ui is not responsible for pedagogy; it only has to not stand in the way of rich instructional design.

retrofit_order._authority: The ordered pipeline when the material already exists. course-factory/retrofit/GUIDE.md is the lane; this is the order.
retrofit_order._law: Content locked, delivery free. retrofit/knowledge/content-lock.json is the authority on which is which.

steps.blocked_without: nothing - if it cannot be determined, say UNKNOWN and ask once

steps.does: programme, ILO map, Track A hours - READ, never rewritten by a retrofit
steps.note: if the existing module is the only record of the hours, say so

steps.does: classify_module.py -> A, B or C, decided here and not asked of the operator
steps.note: on delivery quality only. Valid HTML, resolving links and green checks are not signals

steps.does: what the module teaches, screen by screen, and what each screen CLAIMS - this is what survives
canonical shell, tokens, composition vocabulary, engine, navigation
steps.note: necessary and never sufficient - a retrofit that stops here validates and still looks like a different product

steps.does: every substantial teaching screen gets a representation review; build the stronger representation where the evidence supports it
steps.note: do not report 'animation recommended' when the evidence is enough to build it

steps.does: a composition per screen from the vocabulary; split, merge or add screens as the learning needs
steps.note: minutes are locked, screens are not

steps.does: only when the module has tasks - the task surface, mechanics preserved, presentation free
every new-build check, plus check_language.py and a re-classification
